editorial:
Imagine spending your days around death and silence, only to find that the living are the ones who are truly complicated. You follow a quiet man working as an undertaker who sees the world through a very specific, lonely lens. The vibe here is slow and thoughtful, focusing on the small moments of a man's life that most people would ignore. It feels like you are eavesdropping on a private conversation, watching a character try to figure out how to connect with others while he spends most of his time with people who cannot talk back.

What really works is the acting; the lead keeps things grounded and real without overacting. The pacing is definitely slow, so if you love high-energy action, this might feel a bit sluggish for you. However, the honest look at grief and loneliness makes it worth your time. You should definitely try to find this in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video if you can, or just rent it on Apple TV for a cozy night in. If you are a collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical shelf is a great way to keep this artistic piece of cinema forever.
endingExplained: The story wraps up with the main character finally accepting that he cannot hide from the world forever. In the final scenes, he has a breakthrough that allows him to let go of his sadness. He stops treating his job as a shield and starts opening up to the people around him. It ends on a hopeful note, showing that even someone who deals with death every day can find a reason to start living again.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character studies and quiet stories about life.
